wool-sweater.title: Visible Mended Sweater Elbows
wool-sweater.summary: Strengthen thin sweater elbows using contrast thread stitching to extend the garment life.
steps: Turn the sweater inside out to find the thin patches near the elbows.
Thread your needle with a double strand of contrasting thread.
Stitch small parallel vertical lines across the thin area 5 mm apart.
Weave horizontal lines over and under the vertical lines to form a woven patch.
Secure the thread on the inside with a small knot.
wool-sweater.fabricReason: Wool knit takes hand darning well, allowing contrast thread to blend into the weave seamlessly.
warnings: Hot water and rubbing will felt and shrink wool. Only do it on purpose.
wool-sweater.menderBrief: Darn the elbow areas using a visible woven patch technique. Use sturdy contrast thread and secure all ends tightly.

wool-sweater.title: Felted Wool Cuff Mittens
wool-sweater.summary: Turn the lower sleeves and cuffs into warm fingerless mittens.
steps: Wash the sweater in hot water to purposely felt the wool so it will not unravel.
Cut 20 cm off the bottom of each sleeve using scissors.
Try on the sleeve pieces with the ribbed cuff at your wrist.
Mark a 3 cm gap for your thumb on the side seam.
Stitch the side seam above and below the thumb opening using needle and thread.
wool-sweater.fabricReason: Felted wool knit creates a dense fabric that keeps hands warm and will not fray when cut.
warnings: Felting with a hot wash: shrinks the wool a lot, only do it on purpose.
wool-sweater.menderBrief: Felt the sleeve ends first to prevent unraveling. Cut two wrist warmers from the lower sleeves and leave a clean side opening for the thumb.

wool-sweater.title: Sweater Body Cushion Cover
wool-sweater.summary: Transform the main torso of the sweater into a soft, cozy cushion cover.
steps: Stitch two rows of small running stitches 5 mm apart straight across the chest, from armpit to armpit.
Cut just above the stitched rows to remove the top of the sweater.
Turn the body piece inside out.
Sew the top cut edge completely closed using needle and thread with a strong backstitch.
Insert a 40x40 cm cushion pad through the open bottom hem.
Sew the bottom hem closed with small neat stitches.
wool-sweater.fabricReason: Wool sweater knit provides a thick texture ideal for home furnishings like cushion covers.
warnings: Cutting a knit: stitch twice along the line first so it does not unravel.
wool-sweater.menderBrief: Square off the torso section of the wool sweater. Secure raw cut knit edges with double stitching before hand-sewing the seams to enclose a 40x40 cm cushion pad.

stretch-jeans.title: Raw Hem Cropped Jeans
stretch-jeans.summary: Crop the lower legs of the jeans to create a modern raw hem finish.
steps: Try on the jeans and mark your desired new length with chalk.
Lay the jeans flat on a smooth surface and line up the inseams.
Cut straight across both legs 1 cm below your mark using sharp scissors.
Use your fingers to pull at the cut threads to create a soft frayed edge.
Wash the jeans to set the fringe finish along the cut line.
stretch-jeans.fabricReason: Woven denim frays easily when cut, making it ideal for a quick raw hem project.
warnings: Heavy fraying: finish cut edges or make the fray part of the design.
stretch-jeans.menderBrief: Crop the jean legs 1 cm below the target mark using scissors. Pull the crosswise threads manually to establish a uniform 1 cm raw hem fringe.

stretch-jeans.title: Jean Pocket Wall Organiser
stretch-jeans.summary: Remove the back pockets and sew them onto a panel cut from the jean leg to store small tools.
steps: Cut a wide rectangular panel from the cleanest section of one jean leg.
Carefully cut out the two back pockets from the jeans leaving a 1 cm border.
Finish all four edges of the large denim panel using a zigzag stitch.
Position the pockets onto the panel and pin them in place.
Stitch around the sides and bottom of each pocket onto the panel, reinforcing the top corners.
stretch-jeans.fabricReason: Sturdy cotton denim holds its shape well when used to construct utility organisers.
warnings: Stretch fabric: use a stretch stitch or ballpoint needle, do not pull while sewing.
stretch-jeans.menderBrief: Construct a rectangular denim wall hanging panel with zigzagged edges. Mount the removed back pockets using reinforced top tacking.

stretch-jeans.title: Straight Cut Denim Tote Bag
stretch-jeans.summary: Turn the main body of the jeans into a durable tote bag with straps made from the legs.
steps: Cut off both legs of the jeans straight across just below the crotch seam.
Turn the upper body section inside out and stitch the bottom cut opening closed.
Cut two long strips from the legs to form 4 cm wide shoulder straps.
Fold and topstitch the straps along both long edges for strength.
Stitch the ends of the straps securely inside the waistband on the front and back.
stretch-jeans.fabricReason: Denim provides excellent structure and durability for a daily carry bag.
warnings: Machine sewing across several denim layers: use a denim needle (100/16 or 110/18) and go slowly.
Heavy fraying: finish cut edges or make the fray part of the design.
stretch-jeans.menderBrief: Convert the upper section of the jeans into a tote bag by closing the bottom cut edge with a reinforced seam. Attach double-stitched straps cut from the legs inside the original waistband.

cotton-shirt.title: Raw Edge Cropped Shirt
cotton-shirt.summary: Crop the lower body of the shirt to create a modern short shirt with a deliberately frayed raw hem.
steps: Try on the shirt and mark the desired crop height using chalk.
Lay the shirt flat on a hard surface and smooth out all wrinkles.
Cut straight across the marked line using sharp scissors.
Press the new raw edge flat with an iron on high heat.
Gently pull at the cut threads to create a uniform 2 mm frayed border.
cotton-shirt.fabricReason: Woven cotton frays neatly when cut, making it ideal for deliberate raw-edge designs.
warnings: Raw edges will continue to fray slightly over time when washed.
cotton-shirt.menderBrief: Crop the lower hem of the shirt using scissors to create a deliberate raw-edge look. Press the new bottom hem flat and gently pull edge threads to create a clean, intentional fray.

cotton-shirt.title: No-Sew Tied Tote Bag
cotton-shirt.summary: Transform the body of the shirt into a functional tote bag using a simple cut-and-tie fringe method.
steps: Cut off the sleeves and the neck collar following the inner seams.
Turn the shirt inside out and align the front and back bottom edges.
Cut vertical strips along the bottom hem measuring 2 cm wide and 8 cm long through both layers.
Knot each front strip securely to its corresponding back strip across the entire bottom.
Turn the bag right side out and press the straps flat with an iron.
cotton-shirt.fabricReason: Sturdy woven cotton holds structure well and creates durable knots at the bottom of the bag.
warnings: Unfinished cut edges along the straps and fringe may fray with heavy use.
cotton-shirt.menderBrief: Convert the shirt into a no-sew tote bag by removing the sleeves and collar. Cut matching 8 cm fringe strips at the bottom hem and double-knot front and back strips together to form the base.

cotton-shirt.title: Glued Appliqué Patch Shirt
cotton-shirt.summary: Use fabric from the cut sleeves to create decorative appliqué patches on the front pocket or chest area.
steps: Cut off one sleeve and lay the fabric completely flat.
Trace a geometric shape onto paper and cut out the template.
Use the template to cut out two matching fabric shapes from the sleeve.
Fold 5 mm along all edges of the fabric shapes and press flat with an iron.
Apply fabric glue evenly to the folded edges and press firmly onto the shirt chest.
Iron the glued area for 30 seconds to help set the adhesive bond.
cotton-shirt.fabricReason: Woven cotton responds well to pressing crisp 5 mm folds, which keeps glued edges neat.
warnings: Cut edges must be folded under before gluing, or heavy fraying will occur in the wash.
cotton-shirt.menderBrief: Create geometric appliqué patches using fabric cut from the shirt sleeve. Fold under all patch edges by 5 mm, press flat, and secure to the main shirt using fabric glue.

acrylic-sweater.title: Embroidered Neckline Accent
acrylic-sweater.summary: Add simple decorative hand-embroidered stitches around the existing sweater neckline.
steps: Thread your needle with a double strand of thread and knot the end.
Begin stitching simple straight stitches along the ribbed neckline seam.
Work your way around the entire neck opening keeping stitches evenly spaced.
Secure the thread inside the garment with a double knot.
acrylic-sweater.fabricReason: Acrylic knit holds surface embroidery well without distorting if stitches are kept loose.
warnings: Acrylic melts under a hot iron. Keep heat away from it.
Stretch fabric: do not pull thread too tightly or the neck ribbing will pucker.
acrylic-sweater.menderBrief: Add simple decorative hand embroidery around the garment neckline. Ensure tension is loose to allow the knit to stretch.

acrylic-sweater.title: Cinched Button Cuffs
acrylic-sweater.summary: Fold and sew decorative buttons onto the wrists to gather and cinch the sleeves.
steps: Pinch a small 2 cm fold on the upper side of one sleeve cuff.
Thread your needle and anchor the thread inside the cuff fold.
Sew a button directly over the pinch to secure the fold flat.
Repeat the exact same pinch and button attachment on the second cuff.
acrylic-sweater.fabricReason: The soft acrylic knit easily folds into neat pleats without adding heavy bulk.
warnings: Acrylic melts under a hot iron. Keep heat away from it.
Stretch fabric: stitch firmly through all layers of the fold to prevent stretching out.
acrylic-sweater.menderBrief: Create a decorative pleat at each sleeve cuff and secure it in place by sewing a button over the fold.

acrylic-sweater.title: Sew-On Patch Accents
acrylic-sweater.summary: Stitch fabric patches onto the elbows or chest using basic hand stitches.
steps: Place the sweater flat and position one patch over the desired area.
Anchor your thread inside the sweater body under the patch edge.
Use a catch stitch or whip stitch around the full perimeter of the patch.
Knot the thread securely on the inside of the sweater.
Repeat the process for the second patch on the opposite side.
acrylic-sweater.fabricReason: Acrylic sweaters provide a thick stable base for securing applique patches by hand.
warnings: Acrylic melts under a hot iron. Keep heat away from it.
Stretch fabric: keep stitches relaxed so the knit can stretch when worn.
acrylic-sweater.menderBrief: Hand stitch two applique patches onto the sweater body or sleeves using a neat catch stitch. Maintain fabric flexibility.
